steps.title: Normal pressure profile
steps.body: Typical readings: access −50 mmHg, pre-filter ~180 mmHg, return ~80 mmHg, TMP ~120 mmHg at blood flow 150 mL/min. Know your patient's baseline.
steps.tip: Sudden TMP rise often precedes clotting — act before complete circuit loss.

steps.title: Access pressure alarm
steps.body: Access pressure more negative than −150 mmHg suggests catheter malfunction, kinking, or inadequate blood flow from the vein.
steps.tip: Check line position, reverse lines if recirculation suspected, consider catheter exchange.

steps.title: Return pressure alarm
steps.body: Return pressure >250 mmHg may indicate clot in filter/line, elevated hematocrit, or return line obstruction.
steps.tip: Reduce blood flow temporarily while evaluating; prepare circuit change.

steps.title: TMP and filter life
steps.body: TMP >200 mmHg is a warning; >300 mmHg often mandates circuit change. Regional citrate anticoagulation can extend filter life beyond 24–72 h.
steps.tip: See full NephroGuide CRRT tool for citrate dosing and monitoring.
